text.p: Mexican industrial firm Alfa SA said on Thursday its 1996 profits of 3.928 billion pesos, reported earlier in the day, were "excellent."

"Significant increases in sales volumes have enabled ALFA to reach record-high levels of revenues and EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization). We will continue reinvesting these resources, to acheive more profitable growth in forthcoming years," said chairman Dionisio Garza Medina.

Alfa reported net profits of 3.928 billion pesos compared to a 1995 net of 2.218 billion. Much of the difference was due to an integrated financial gain, which includes non-cash items, of 1.449 billion pesos.

Alfa's net sales rose by 1.2 percent compared to 1995 levels. Average volume increased by 12.9 percent and was partly offset by a 10.3 percent decline in real prices in pesos, the Monterrey-based firm said.
During the fourth quarter alone, Alfa's net sales jumped 4.6 percent compared to the third quarter. Sales volume increased 9.9 percent to compensate for a 4.9 percent fall in prices.

Domestic sales increased 18.6 percent to 20.355 billion pesos, while exports fell 19.8 percent to $1.105 billion. As a percentage of sales, exports in peso terms decreased to 26.9 percent from 37.6 percent, due to higher domestic sales, lower petrochemical prices and a stronger peso.

Alfa's operating income was up 2.7 percent on 1995 levels. "On a consolidated basis, revenue growth and a better cost structure allowed Alfa to post better operating results than last year, despite the negative effects of a stronger peso and reduced international prices for petrochemical products," the company said.
Operating income during the fourth quarter alone was virtually flat compared to the third quarter, it said.

The company raised its 1996 operating margin to 16.7 percent from 16.4 percent in 1995. Operating margin during the fourth quarter was 16.0 percent, down from 16.8 percent in the third quarter due to higher costs and operating expenses in Alpek and Sigma units.
